missions.title: Third-Party Support Widget
missions.summary: Review a browser support feature that combines cross-window messaging, DOM rendering and a loaded client dependency.
missions.story: A support widget receives browser messages and displays replies inside an authenticated application page. Compare the deployed behavior with a repaired implementation.

review.title: Support widget review route
review.visibleBehavior: The prepared strong element is interpreted and rendered as markup.

repaired.title: Support widget repaired route
repaired.visibleBehavior: The same markup-shaped value is displayed literally as text.

objectives.title: Discover the trust boundary
objectives.summary: Inspect the deployed widget and identify the browser behavior that deserves investigation.
instructions: Open the review target and inspect its loaded dependency and widget source.
Compare the browser-message input with the operation that updates the conversation preview.
Choose the observation that best describes the security boundary.
objectives.hint: Follow data from the message event into the conversation preview and note the loaded library version.
objectives.demoCue: Show that code, runtime behavior and the loaded dependency are three views of one browser feature.

options.label: Browser-message content is interpreted as HTML by an older dependency.
The support button uses a strong visual style.
The page and widget share the same route origin.

objectives.title: Prove the browser behavior
objectives.summary: Trigger one harmless prepared browser message and collect deterministic visible evidence.
instructions: Open the review target in a separate tab.
Press Send support reply and observe whether the prepared strong element becomes DOM markup.
Enter the evidence token shown by the target.
objectives.hint: The token appears only after the target finds the prepared marker inside the rendered support thread.
objectives.demoCue: Run the same button action while IAST is active, then correlate the visible marker with runtime evidence.

objectives.title: Validate the repair
objectives.summary: Repeat the feature on the repaired route and verify that functionality remains without HTML interpretation.
instructions: Open the repaired target and repeat Send support reply.
Confirm that the markup-shaped content is displayed literally.
Inspect the strict origin, payload-type and text-rendering controls, then enter the remediation token.
objectives.hint: The repaired route keeps the same user action but validates the message and writes text rather than HTML.
objectives.demoCue: Compare the dependency versions and the two source files, then show that the safe route preserves the feature.

missions.title: Deployment Response Boundary
missions.summary: Compare two visually identical deployments whose security difference exists only in browser-observed response metadata.
missions.story: An account console looks identical in review and repaired deployments. One response discloses its server technology while the repaired response preserves the same page and security baseline without the disclosure.

review.title: Deployment response with metadata disclosure
review.visibleBehavior: The page matches the repaired control, but inspecting its response reveals a technology disclosure header.

repaired.title: Deployment response without metadata disclosure
repaired.visibleBehavior: The same page and security baseline are returned without the technology disclosure header.

objectives.title: Look beyond the rendered page
objectives.summary: Identify why identical page content does not imply identical security posture.
instructions: Start the route-aware server and open both deployment targets.
Confirm that their rendered content is identical.
Choose the browser evidence that must be compared.
objectives.hint: The meaningful difference travels with the HTTP response rather than appearing in the DOM.
objectives.demoCue: Show both identical pages first, then move to the browser-observed response metadata to explain why source-only inspection is incomplete.

options.label: Their HTTP response metadata.
Their visible page headings.
Their button presentation.

objectives.title: Prove the disclosure
objectives.summary: Inspect the review response and collect deterministic evidence from the browser.
instructions: Open the review target through the route-aware server.
Press Inspect response metadata.
Enter the evidence token displayed by the target.
objectives.hint: The review response contains one additional technology-identifying header.
objectives.demoCue: Run passive DAST while loading the route, then correlate the finding with the target's harmless response-inspection proof.

objectives.title: Validate the repaired response
objectives.summary: Verify that the disclosure is gone without changing page behavior or the secure header baseline.
instructions: Open the repaired target through the route-aware server.
Press Inspect response metadata and confirm the disclosure header is absent.
Enter the repaired evidence token.
objectives.hint: The paired response keeps the same body and security headers while removing only the technology disclosure.
objectives.demoCue: Use the repaired route as a negative oracle: identical functionality, same secure baseline and no disclosure finding.

missions.title: Session-Bound Order Search
missions.summary: Capture and test a same-origin POST request that only exists after the browser establishes scoped session state.
missions.story: An account console searches the current user's orders through a form-encoded POST request. The browser establishes the session and request context; the review API exposes a database error under malformed input while the repaired API preserves the workflow safely.

productPreview.label: PTK Pro
productPreview.summary: Additional active browser-request coverage is being developed for a future release.

review.title: Order search review workflow

request.setup: Open the review page to establish its scoped session and submit the search form.

review.visibleBehavior: A normal order search succeeds; the harmless prepared diagnostic exposes a database-query error.

repaired.title: Order search repaired workflow

request.setup: Open the repaired page to establish its scoped session and submit the same search form.

repaired.visibleBehavior: The same normal and diagnostic searches complete without exposing a database-query error.

objectives.title: Capture the real browser request
objectives.summary: Identify the request context that a URL-only scanner would not possess.
instructions: Open the review workflow through the route-aware server.
Submit the normal order search and inspect the browser request.
Choose the evidence needed to replay the same operation.
objectives.hint: The API is not a useful standalone URL: the page establishes a scoped session and creates the form-encoded request.
objectives.demoCue: Start DAST before submitting the normal form and show how browser traffic provides the method, body, session and request context together.

options.label: Its captured method, body and scoped browser session.
The API pathname by itself.
The visible account-console title.

objectives.title: Prove the server-side weakness
objectives.summary: Use the prepared diagnostic to expose a deterministic database error inside the scoped session.
instructions: Open the review workflow and first submit the normal search.
Press Run prepared diagnostic.
Enter the evidence token displayed by the target.
objectives.hint: The prepared input changes only the query value while preserving the captured request context.
objectives.demoCue: Correlate the active DAST finding with the review API's deterministic error response without exposing or changing private scanner payloads.

objectives.title: Validate the repaired query path
objectives.summary: Repeat the identical browser workflow and confirm that malformed data is handled without a database error.
instructions: Open the repaired workflow and submit the normal search.
Run the same prepared diagnostic.
Enter the repaired evidence token.
objectives.hint: The repaired route keeps the same page, session, method, headers and body shape; only server-side query handling changes.
objectives.demoCue: Use the repaired route as a negative oracle and verify that active DAST does not inherit the review finding.

missions.title: On-Demand Analytics
missions.summary: Observe a client dependency that does not exist in initial page traffic and appears only after a browser action opens an application feature.
missions.story: An account page keeps its analytics workspace dormant until the user opens it. That action loads a same-origin client dependency; compare the deployed version with the reviewed replacement while preserving the same feature.

review.title: Analytics workspace review route
review.visibleBehavior: The initial page is dependency-free; opening the workspace requests and runs the pinned review dependency.

repaired.title: Analytics workspace repaired route
repaired.visibleBehavior: The same action and analytics result are preserved while the browser loads the reviewed dependency version.

objectives.title: Observe the initial dependency boundary
objectives.summary: Establish why a page-load-only inventory misses part of this application's browser attack surface.
instructions: Open the review target without pressing its workspace button.
Inspect the initial browser traffic and confirm that the analytics dependency has not been requested.
Choose the action needed to observe the complete client dependency set.
objectives.hint: The analytics feature is dormant until the application user opens its workspace.
objectives.demoCue: Start with the quiet initial page and show why package files present in browser traffic can depend on a real user journey.

options.label: Open the analytics workspace and observe the new script request.
Reload the untouched page repeatedly.
Read the visible page title.

objectives.title: Prove the action-loaded component
objectives.summary: Load the review workspace and collect deterministic evidence that its dependency executed.
instructions: Start composition analysis before triggering the feature.
Press Open analytics workspace and observe the new same-origin dependency request.
Enter the evidence token displayed after the analytics summary renders.
objectives.hint: The evidence token appears only after the requested dependency executes and updates the workspace.
objectives.demoCue: Correlate the new script request and loaded component finding with the visible analytics result, without relying on a static package manifest.

objectives.title: Validate the reviewed replacement
objectives.summary: Repeat the same browser journey and verify that the feature works with the reviewed dependency.
instructions: Open the repaired target with a new composition-analysis session.
Press Open analytics workspace and confirm that the same summary is rendered.
Enter the repaired evidence token and compare the loaded component versions.
objectives.hint: The repaired target changes the dependency version, not the user action or analytics output.
objectives.demoCue: Use the repaired route as a negative advisory oracle while showing that the browser feature remains intact.

missions.title: Saved Workspace
missions.summary: Follow user-controlled browser state from a settings page into a separate same-origin dashboard document.
missions.story: A team member saves a dashboard announcement in workspace settings. A child dashboard route restores that origin-scoped state; compare markup interpretation with a repaired text-rendering path while preserving the two-document workflow.

productPreview.label: PTK Pro
productPreview.summary: Additional advanced analysis for persistent browser state has completed initial validation for a future release.

review.title: Saved workspace review journey

journey.summary: Save the prepared announcement and follow the same-origin dashboard navigation.

review.visibleBehavior: The settings page persists a harmless markup-shaped value; the child dashboard restores it as DOM markup.

repaired.title: Saved workspace repaired journey

journey.summary: Save the same prepared announcement and follow the same-origin dashboard navigation.

repaired.visibleBehavior: The same state and navigation are preserved while the child dashboard restores the value as literal text.

objectives.title: Discover the cross-document source
objectives.summary: Identify the browser state that survives navigation and becomes input to a new document.
instructions: Open the review setup route and inspect the save action.
Follow the prepared announcement from the settings form into origin-scoped storage and the child dashboard.
Choose the evidence boundary that connects the two documents.
objectives.hint: The dashboard does not receive the announcement in its URL or response body; it reads state left by the previous document.
objectives.demoCue: Show the clean dashboard URL first, then trace the saved value across navigation to explain why browser state matters.

completion.prompt: What connects the settings page to the dashboard sink?

options.label: Origin-scoped browser storage restored by the child document.
A value embedded in the dashboard URL.
A response header sent by the dashboard server.

objectives.title: Prove the persisted rendering path
objectives.summary: Save the prepared value, follow the child navigation and observe how the new document renders it.
instructions: Start runtime analysis on the review setup route.
Press Save and open dashboard, allowing the browser to navigate to the child route.
Enter the evidence token displayed after the dashboard restores the saved value.
objectives.hint: The token appears when the restored strong element exists in the child dashboard DOM.
objectives.demoCue: Correlate the visible element with static source evidence and the runtime storage-to-DOM flow across navigation.

objectives.title: Validate safe restoration
objectives.summary: Repeat the same two-document journey and verify that the saved value remains literal text.
instructions: Open the repaired setup route and keep the prepared announcement unchanged.
Save it and follow the same child-dashboard navigation.
Confirm that the markup-shaped value is displayed literally, then enter the repaired token.
objectives.hint: The storage mechanism and navigation are unchanged; only the dashboard's DOM write is repaired.
objectives.demoCue: Compare the two small dashboard sources and show that the application workflow remains intact without markup interpretation.

missions.title: Live Profile Preview
missions.summary: Follow a same-origin JSON response field into a DOM rendering path that exists only after a browser action.
missions.story: An account page keeps profile data out of initial traffic until a user opens its live preview. Compare the deployed response-to-DOM path with a repaired text-rendering path while preserving the endpoint, response and browser action.

review.title: Live profile review target

action.summary: Press Open live profile preview and wait for the response status.

review.visibleBehavior: The initial page has no profile traffic; the action loads a JSON field and interprets its harmless markup in the preview.

repaired.title: Live profile repaired control

action.summary: Press the same preview button and wait for the response status.

repaired.visibleBehavior: The same action and JSON response are preserved while its markup-shaped field is displayed as literal text.

objectives.title: Discover the response boundary
objectives.summary: Identify why initial page traffic and a standalone source file do not prove the complete browser flow.
instructions: Open the review target without pressing its preview button.
Confirm that the profile JSON has not been requested, then inspect the button's response-to-rendering path.
Choose the browser evidence needed to connect the API field to the visible preview.
objectives.hint: The response exists only after the feature is opened, and the important value is one field inside its parsed JSON body.
objectives.demoCue: Begin with an empty network view, then open the feature to correlate new browser traffic, source and runtime evidence.

completion.prompt: What proves the complete data path?

options.label: The browser action, parsed response field and resulting DOM write.
The account page title by itself.
The JSON pathname without executing the feature.

objectives.title: Prove response-field reachability
objectives.summary: Open the review preview and collect deterministic evidence that the response field became DOM markup.
instructions: Start static and runtime analysis on the review target.
Press Open live profile preview and observe the same-origin JSON request.
Enter the evidence token shown after the prepared marker becomes a DOM element.
objectives.hint: The token appears only when the marker from the parsed JSON field exists as an element in the preview.
objectives.demoCue: Correlate the visible marker with the exact response field and sink instead of treating every response or DOM write as equivalent.

objectives.title: Validate text-only rendering
objectives.summary: Repeat the same action and response while confirming that the response field remains literal text.
instructions: Open the repaired target and press the same profile-preview button.
Confirm that it requests the same JSON document and displays the same response bytes as text.
Enter the repaired evidence token.
objectives.hint: The endpoint, JSON field and browser action are unchanged; only the final DOM write differs.
objectives.demoCue: Compare the two small scripts and prove that the user flow survives without interpreting the response field as markup.

missions.title: Transient Route Notice
missions.summary: Observe a short-lived SPA deep-link value that reaches the DOM after an in-document hash-route change.
missions.story: An incident workspace accepts a notice through its client-side route and removes it almost immediately. Compare a transient markup-rendering path with an allow-listed text-only repair while preserving the same action, route parameter and expiry boundary.

review.title: Transient route notice review target

action.summary: Press Open prepared route notice and scan the resulting hash-query route.

review.visibleBehavior: The action changes only the fragment route; its harmless notice becomes markup for 30 ms before expiring.

repaired.title: Transient route notice repaired control

action.summary: Press the same button and scan the resulting hash-query route.

repaired.visibleBehavior: The same known route value maps to constant text for 30 ms; unknown values are rejected without reflection.

objectives.title: Discover the in-document route boundary
objectives.summary: Identify why an initial response or persistent DOM snapshot can miss the important browser behavior.
instructions: Open the review target and confirm that its initial URL has no route notice.
Press Open prepared route notice and observe the hash-query change without a document reload.
Choose the evidence needed to understand the short-lived rendering path.
objectives.hint: The response document does not change; the browser route and DOM change briefly inside the existing page.
objectives.demoCue: Keep the network and DOM views visible to show that a real browser sees an application transition that a response-only scanner can miss.

options.label: The hash-route mutation and DOM changes observed during the live page transition.
Only the initial HTML response body.
A DOM snapshot taken after the notice has expired.

objectives.title: Prove the transient route flow
objectives.summary: Trigger the deep link and collect evidence while the route-controlled markup exists only briefly.
instructions: Start browser traffic, static and runtime analysis on the review target.
Press Open prepared route notice and scan the resulting hash-query parameter.
Enter the persistent evidence token after the visible notice has expired.
objectives.hint: The notice itself lasts 30 ms, but the proof token records that the prepared marker became an element.
objectives.demoCue: Correlate the SPA attack, static source-to-sink path and runtime hash-query flow around one browser action.

objectives.title: Validate allow-listed text rendering
objectives.summary: Repeat the same route action and expiry while verifying that arbitrary values are not reflected.
instructions: Open the repaired target and press the same route-notice button.
Confirm that the known value displays as text and an unexpected route value is rejected.
Enter the repaired evidence token.
objectives.hint: The action, parameter and 30 ms expiry are unchanged; the application maps one accepted value to constant text.
objectives.demoCue: Show that the repair preserves the normal SPA workflow while providing a clean active and runtime control.

missions.title: Imported Request Preferences
missions.summary: Trace a user-imported client configuration into an inherited browser request option, then compare an own-property allow-list repair.
missions.story: An account preview imports a small JSON preferences document before loading a same-origin resource. Compare an unsafe object merge that creates an inherited request option with a null-prototype allow-list that preserves the same user action and request.
missions.evidenceSummary: Imported data changes inherited request options

productPreview.label: PTK Pro
productPreview.summary: Additional advanced analysis for imported client configuration has completed initial validation for a future release.

review.title: Imported preferences review target

action.summary: Press Import and load preview, then inspect the request-options evidence.

review.visibleBehavior: The imported document leaves the request object with no own credentials key, but its inherited value changes the same-origin preview request.

repaired.title: Imported preferences repaired control

action.summary: Press the same import button and inspect the repaired request-options evidence.

repaired.visibleBehavior: The same input and preview request use a null-prototype object containing only an accepted own credentials option.

objectives.title: Discover the configuration boundary
objectives.summary: Identify how a harmless-looking imported object can change request behavior without adding an own option key.
instructions: Open the review target and inspect the prepared JSON before importing it.
Follow the parsed object through the merge and into the preview request options.
Choose the browser evidence that reveals the complete behavior.
objectives.hint: Compare the object's own keys with the value the browser reads through its prototype chain.
objectives.demoCue: Show the clean list of own request keys first, then the inherited option used by the live request.

completion.prompt: What reveals the configuration integrity problem?

options.label: The difference between own option keys and the inherited value read by the request.
The text returned by the preview endpoint by itself.
The wording of the import button.

objectives.title: Prove the inherited request option
objectives.summary: Import the prepared document and correlate its merge with the resulting same-origin request.
instructions: Start static and runtime analysis on the review target.
Press Import and load preview and observe the one local JSON request.
Enter the evidence token shown when the request option exists only through inheritance.
objectives.hint: The request object reports no own credentials key even though reading the property returns include.
objectives.demoCue: Correlate the static merge path, runtime prototype write and the browser request that consumes the inherited field.

objectives.title: Validate reviewed own properties
objectives.summary: Repeat the import while proving that inherited, dangerous and unknown keys cannot become request options.
instructions: Open the repaired target and import the same prepared document.
Confirm that the request options have no prototype and contain only an own reviewed credentials key.
Try the prepared unknown-key variation, then enter the repaired token.
objectives.hint: The repaired builder copies only accepted own values and supplies a constant safe default.
objectives.demoCue: Show that the preview still loads while arbitrary and inherited input no longer controls request options.

repaired.visibleBehavior: The same route and request use an allow-listed identifier, constant text, and a clean API response.

objectives.title: Discover the route-to-request boundary
objectives.summary: Identify the evidence created only after the SPA action.

Compare the changed route, live DOM and captured JSON request.
objectives.hint: The important view and request do not exist in the initial HTML response.

options.label: The route transition, live DOM update and resulting JSON request.
Only the initial HTML response.
Only the document title.

objectives.title: Prove the browser-created flow
objectives.summary: Correlate route state, DOM behavior and the scoped active request.
instructions: Start browser traffic, static and runtime analysis on the review target.
Press Open prepared order and capture the JSON POST.
Enter the evidence token shown by the in-document route.
objectives.hint: Use the local route-aware runtime when you want to attack the captured API parameter.
objectives.demoCue: Show how one browser action gives SAST, IAST and DAST complementary evidence.

objectives.title: Validate the paired repair

missions.title: Lazy Analytics Route

objectives.title: Establish the quiet initial state

Choose the transition needed to expose the real client surface.

missions.title: Related Child Tab
missions.summary: Continue analysis in a causally related same-origin tab while preserving an explicit different-origin scope boundary.
missions.story: A support launcher opens a same-origin child workspace. The child loads its own dependency and context response before receiving a structured browser message; compare permissive HTML handling and response disclosure with exact validation, text rendering, a reviewed component, and a clean response.
missions.evidenceSummary: Same-origin child message, dependency and response

review.title: Related child-tab review journey

journey.summary: Open the prepared child and inspect evidence in the new same-origin tab.

review.visibleBehavior: The related child loads jQuery 3.4.1, accepts the workspace message as HTML, and receives a response metadata disclosure locally.

repaired.title: Related child-tab repaired journey

journey.summary: Open the paired child and inspect evidence in the new same-origin tab.

repaired.visibleBehavior: The related child validates its opener, loads jQuery 3.7.1, renders text, and receives a clean local response.

objectives.title: Discover the related browser context
objectives.summary: Identify why the launcher tab is not the whole authorised application journey.
instructions: Start on the review launcher and note its origin.
Open the prepared related child and compare its origin and opener relationship.
Observe which code, dependency and request exist only in the child.
objectives.hint: Causality and exact origin both matter; a random same-origin tab is not automatically related.
objectives.demoCue: Keep launcher and child visible, then contrast the optional alternate-host control locally.

completion.prompt: Which tab belongs to the journey?

options.label: The same-origin child opened by the tracked launcher.
Every unrelated tab that happens to share a hostname.
The alternate-host control with no application state.

objectives.title: Prove child-owned evidence

instructions: Start all browser engines on the review launcher.
Open the related child and wait for its dependency, request and message.
Enter the evidence token displayed inside the child.
objectives.hint: The proof token appears only in the child document after its own lifecycle runs.
objectives.demoCue: Show that the browser journey—not one tab ID—is the useful security boundary.

objectives.title: Validate trust and scope controls
objectives.summary: Preserve the related child while validating its exact message and dependency boundaries.
instructions: Open the repaired launcher and its related child.
Confirm the message is displayed literally and the reviewed dependency loads.
Use the local alternate-host control only to verify that it receives no state, then enter the repaired token.
objectives.hint: The repaired application still follows its child; it does not broaden ownership to the alternate-host control.
